course_name_original: Spanish B2 course - compulsory course of 135 hours for students of FIRST-CYCLE studies - semester 3/3
course_name_en: Spanish B2 course - compulsory course of 135 hours for students of FIRST-CYCLE studies - semester 3/3
prerequisites: Knowledge of Spanish at least at A-2 level.

learning_outcomes.text: Able to write an understandable informative and argumentative text on general and industry-specific topics, conduct correspondence typical of the work environment, and independently use didactic materials.
Able to clearly present conclusions and opinions on general, academic, and professional topics in written and oral form.

Understands longer, even complex written and oral statements, e.g., lectures and presentations, provided they concern industry-specific issues and current affairs, and can interpret the acquired information.

Able to use grammatical structures, phraseology, and vocabulary that allow understanding general texts describing contemporary economic and social phenomena, academic, and industry-specific texts, and allow for fairly fluent and spontaneous communication in academic and professional environments.
Able to prepare an oral presentation on academic and industry-specific topics and participate fairly fluently and spontaneously in discussions, including in a professional environment.

syllabus_topics: Noun: Verbal nouns, Nouns derived from adjectives.

Personal pronoun: functions, omission, order, form (as subject for clarity, emphasis, opposition; as direct object, allowed forms; use when direct object precedes verb; as indirect object; use despite noun presence, duplication in evaluative constructions; with prepositions (entre, excepto, salvo, incluso, hasta segun + pron.pers. sujeto); order and form of indirect object + direct object).
Reflexive pronoun: functions (use in impersonal sentences; meaning of reciprocity; modification of meaning of some verbs (quedarse, irse, tomarse)).
Adjective: Formation of adjectives with opposite meaning, Compound adjectives, Order of adjective and shortened forms.
Preposition: Use of por and para, Specific use of prepositions in conjunction with some verbs and in prepositional phrases.
Verb: Functions of non-finite forms (infinitivo, infinitivo compuesto, participio, gerundio).
Morphology and uses of indicative tenses [presente, preterito perfecto, preterito indefinido, preterito imperfecto, preterito pluscuamperfecto, futuro simple and futuro compuesto de indicativo].
Morphology and uses of conditional tenses [condicional simple, condicional compuesto].
Morphology and uses of subjunctive mood [presente, preterito perfecto, preterito imperfecto, preterito pluscuamperfecto de subjuntivo].
Passive voice [ser + participio (+ por + agente)].
Use of periphrastic constructions [e.g., Estar + participio, Estar + gerundio, acabar + de + infinit., terminar + de + infinit., volver + a + infinit., llevar + gerundio, ir + gerundio].
Formation of impersonal constructions.
Correlation of tenses in subordinate clauses.
Use of verbs ser, estar, haber.
More important verbs changing meaning depending on voice (e.g., poner/ponerse, quedar/quedarse) and the accompanying word (e.g., ponerse + a, ponerse + de).

Words and expressions: indicating logical connections between parts of a sentence (simple, complex), ensuring coherence of speech (oral or written), reflecting the speaker's attitude to the presented content (in discussion).

Presenting own opinion, providing information from other sources, clarifying, organizing speech and adding new arguments, highlighting a previously given argument, introducing new counterarguments, contrasting elements, ordering information, correcting information, rephrasing, summarizing, explaining/justifying, citing examples, citing reasons.
Expressing assumption, hypothesis, condition, concession, cause, effect.
Defining temporal relations (sequence, precedence, simultaneity, specific moment or period, initial or final moment, duration).
Reported speech: transformation of individual elements of a sentence/utterance; semantics of verbs denoting an act of communication.
Creating comparisons and absolute superlative.
Professional work: requirements, skills, experiences, expectations and concerns, forms of contact with employer and team.
Education: My university, faculty and field of study, subjects and forms of classes.
Student life: learning, norms, duties and limitations, entertainment, additional development opportunities, individual and group work.
Designing products that meet specific requirements (object, place, etc.).
Means and methods of transmitting information in the modern world.
Political and historical events.
Culture: films, performances, readings.
Global problems and problems of local communities.
Cities: history, attractions, infrastructure, culture, gastronomy.
Customs, holidays, local and international traditions.
Travel, tourism, tourism industry.
State of the natural environment.
Pro-health behaviors, physical activity, extreme sports.
Interpersonal relationships and lifestyle: family, friends, formal and informal groups, subcultures.
Psychological reactions to events and challenges, attitude to incomprehensible phenomena.
Language functions and other skills: Creating longer individual utterances (oral or written, informative, argumentative or mixed).
Participation in a conversation with one or many partners (discussion, debate, meeting, job interview).
Providing information, indicating, specifying, defining, describing; asking for information, providing and supplementing information, asking for confirmation and referring to given information.
Asking for opinion/assessment and expressing opinion/assessment.
Expressing approval/disapproval, support or lack of support.
Expressing agreement/disagreement; asking someone for agreement, encouraging agreement.
Showing doubt.
Presenting arguments and counterarguments.
Expressing certainty/obviousness or their absence.
Formulating hypotheses.
Expressing possibility, probability.
Expressing conditions and requirements.
Presenting goals and reasons.
Expressing necessity or need or their absence.
Asking about knowledge of something; expressing knowledge or its absence.
Asking about skills and experiences and presenting them to the interlocutor.
Asking about preferences and interests and presenting them.
Asking about preferences and defining preferences; expressing indifference or lack of preference.
Asking about desires/wishes and presenting them.
Asking about plans and intentions and presenting them.

Asking about emotional experiences and expressing joy, satisfaction, sadness, boredom, surfeit, aversion, anger, indignation, fear, anxiety, concern, sympathy, encouragement, hope, disappointment, resignation, remorse, shame, surprise, wonder, admiration, and pride.
Defining physical sensations.
Giving commands or instructions.
Asking for kindness, for an object, help; offering help in action.
Making a request/application/petition and responding.
Asking for permission, granting consent/not granting consent; forbidding.
Proposing and suggesting solutions, joint actions.
Treating, proposing and inviting; accepting an offer or invitation or refusing.
Advising, warning, threatening.
Reproaching.
Making promises and expressing commitment.
Calming and comforting.
Presenting goals and reasons.
Formulating conditions and requirements.
Editing texts: emails and private and official letters e.g., cover letter, CV, applications, petitions, complaints, reports.
Referring in writing or orally to oral texts (interviews, conversations of general content, as well as popular science statements).
Reading popular science texts with understanding.
Creating and presenting longer oral statements related to the field of study.
assessment_rules: A positive grade from all colloquiums conducted during the semester is required to pass. In case of a negative grade, the student has the right to improve it; the first improvement replaces the negative grade, while a second improvement results in the average of the two grades (which cannot be less than 3.0 for a passed test). Unjustified absence from a test results in forfeiture of the attempt, and students have two retake colloquiums. The final grade is the arithmetic mean of all grades obtained from passing individual semesters and the foreign language exam.
